ModMetaData.name: Yuudong Deep Mining
ModMetaData.author: yuudong2
ModMetaData.description:
Dig down instead of tearing up the mountains around your base.
Build a mine shaft and a brand-new underground level opens up beneath it: solid rock laced with ore veins. Build another shaft down there to go one level deeper.
Features - Mine shaft (2x2): opens a new underground map below it. Build it on the surface or on an underground level. One shaft per map. Maximum depth is configurable (default: 5 levels). - Underground levels are dark cave maps full of rock. The deeper you go, the more ore veins there are and the more valuable the ore gets. - Harder rock: rock and ore get tougher with every level (+50% per level, stops increasing at level 4 by default). - Infestations: underground levels with colonists on them get insect infestations, more often the deeper you go (with a cap). - Colonists work across levels: the normal vanilla work search also looks at the other levels connected by the shaft, and when a job there comes first by your work priorities, colonists climb the ladders to do it. Haulers carry ore and other items up or down to wherever there is storage for them. - One colony across levels: needs work the same way. If a colonist can't eat, sleep in a bed, relax and so on where they are, they go to the level where they can. Doctors carry downed allies to a bed on another level, and you can capture enemies into a prison on another level. Workbenches get their ingredients from storage on other levels. - Alerts, resource counts, "do until you have X" bills and colony wealth count every level of the shaft together. Tamed animals follow their master between levels. - Home level: give each colonist a level to mainly stay on. They go out when there is work or a need elsewhere and come back once idle. - Level panel: switch between levels with the panel at the top right (or the = and - keys). Colonists you had selected stay selected from the other level, so you can right-click to give them any order there, from moving to prioritizing a workbench. They climb the ladders and carry it out when they arrive. - Sealing a shaft, or losing it, collapses every level below it. Everything down there is lost, and anyone still below is buried alive. A sealed shaft stays behind, filled with earth and boarded over; deconstruct it to clear the spot. - Raids: when none of your active colonists are on the surface but some are underground, sapper and breacher raids follow you down the shaft. Other raiders never notice the underground levels. - The shaft only takes damage when it is deliberately attacked: enemy AI never picks it as a target, and stray shots pass over it. The ladder out of an underground level cannot be damaged or deconstructed.
Settings: maximum depth, size of new levels, rock hardness, infestation frequency, sapper/breacher raids following you down, indestructible shafts.
Requirements: RimWorld 1.7 and Harmony. No DLC required. Languages: English, Korean.
Notes - Every underground level is a separate map, so many levels cost performance. - Removing this mod from a save that has underground levels will break the save. - Underground levels are covered by thick overhead mountain everywhere. Mine large areas carefully and leave pillars, or the roof can collapse just like on the surface.
